newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM, ALM Antillean plan more cooperation.
newsitem.headline: KLM, ALM Antillean plan more cooperation.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV and ALM Antillean Airlines NV, in which KLM owns a 40 percent stake, are discussing increased passenger and airfreight cooperation, KLM spokesman Peter Welhuener told Reuters.
He said a memorandum of understanding has been signed by KLM and ALM management.
A joint business plan is to be setup by end-1996 with a new joint venture operation due by April 1 1997, he added.
KLM and ALM already share flight numbers on aircraft bound for the islands of Curacao, Bonaire and Saint Martin in the Dutch Antilles, he said.
The business plan will seek ways of expanding co-operation, based on ALM's on-going negotiation of increased landing rights to South American destinations, Welheuner added.
"The intention of ALM is to expand its routes so you can imagine that an expanding network can be meaningful for air cargo as well as for passenger activities," he said.
He added the two airlines may also cooperate in catering and handling activities, as well as joint marketing of their routes.

KLM's 40 percent stake in ALM is expected to fall to around 25 percent, after the announcement last year by the government of the Dutch Antilles to inject cash into the airline, industry sources said.
The two airlines currently fly 13 times a week to the three islands from Amsterdam using Boeing 747 and McDonnell Douglas MD-11 aircraft. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
